chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"What is prohibited due to lineage is also prohibited due to breastfeeding."
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between marriage prohibitions due to blood and those due to breastfeeding in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* articulates the foundational Shia legal maxim that the degree of prohibition in marriage due to breastfeeding (radāʿ) mirrors that of blood lineage (nasab). It underscores the juristic consensus that milk kinship creates a permanent barrier to marriage, treating the wet nurse and her close relatives as equivalent to biological parents and siblings. This principle is critical in Shia fiqh for determining mahram relationships in cases of fosterage.
